analysis.cluster: Weapon terms: family, damage, delivery, targets, traits
analysis.summary: Coders split on weapon coding mostly because rules were missing or contradicted each other. Nothing said whether a game's damage_map decides the damage field. The rockets / guided-missiles tie-break pushed self-homing rockets into a family whose allowed deliveries forbid them. can_target had no stated meaning: any hit or only useful hits, plus open questions on naval, structures, lock-on weapons and high air in shooters. The helicopter's main-weapon family gap is a slot problem from another group: under decision 2A the pilot's default rockets must be the primary weapon. I propose: one ordered damage rule (repair; no-damage weapons take the family default; registry exceptions; a single mapped game category wins even against the family, recorded as atypical; otherwise the family default, with armour-piercing and explosive exceptions); a source-based rockets / guided tie-break; sharper family tie-breaks (EMP vs magnetic, small arms vs machine gun judged by how it fires, sniper, artillery vs cannon); a delivery fallback to the family default plus a one-attack-one-entry order; a can_target rule split by commanded and piloted games, with naval following ground vehicles; and coding rules for anti-air, suppress, magazine, homing and splash. Under these rules every pilot disagreement in this group resolves to one value, main weapon family and damage rise to 100%, and the RA3 samples need a few fixes (Tanya's guns become small arms, plus naval and structure targets).

proposals.evidence: main weapon.damage 77.8% (below 80%): Terror Drone claws A melee, B explosive (plus a second claws entry with kinetic), C explosive; IFV launcher A explosive, B armour-piercing, C explosive. armament.damage set 87%: Terror Drone A {emp, melee}, B {explosive, kinetic}, C {emp, explosive}. Inside the IFV set: Imperial Warrior laser A energy, B and C kinetic (B and C record weapon-families:laser allowed.damage-types kinetic). Reference: claws melee, launcher explosive, IW laser kinetic (atypical). Part of atypical rules at 68.5% (B and C: blades allowed.damage-types explosive; B: kinetic). 9 of 12 reports hesitated on damage (24 hesitations): damage_map vs family (A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3); the stasis ray does no damage (A, B, C ra3); RA3 Magic is missing from the map (A-ra3, C-ra3); splash plus an anti-armour bonus in one term, with no SC2 map (A, B, C sc2); damage of an air-to-air missile (A, B, C battlefield). Gaps in 5 reports (none, true damage, two damage types). Unclear-rule notes in 7 reports.
proposals.root_cause: No rule says how to choose damage. damage-types says only 'what a hit does'. schemas/game.schema.json damage_map says only 'mapped to our damage types', not whether it binds. A family's allowed.damage-types binds cards but only flags atypicals on researched units. So B and C followed the map (claws explosive or kinetic, atypical), A followed the family and the fiction (melee), and B guessed a category no source gives (IFV 'Rocket' to armour-piercing). The samples contradict each other: the IW laser follows the map against its family (kinetic, atypical), while the drone claws ignore the map (melee). Registry notes pull both ways (Tempest Rising lasers: energy despite Cannon; PS2 VS lasers: kinetic from the map; MechWarrior flamers: fire despite Energy). No rule covers a weapon with different categories by target, a category missing from the map, a weapon that does no damage (x-required-unless still forces a value), or a game with no map where damage shows only as a bonus against armour (SC2).
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs.weapon.properties.damage.description (generated into docs/fields.md as armament[].damage); plus one sentence appended to the description of data/vocab/damage-types.json
proposals.change: New description for armament[].damage: 'What a hit does to the target. Decide in this order and stop at the first step that fits. 1. It heals or repairs: repair. 2. It does no damage at all (it only stuns, pins, slows or marks): its family's default damage. Put the effect in traits and say in the summary that it does no damage. 3. The game's registry note names this kind of weapon and a damage type: that type. 4. The game has a damage_map in data/games.json, and the sources cited for this unit give this weapon one game damage category that the map lists: the mapped type. Use it even when the family's list leaves it out, and record that break in atypical. Never change the family to make the damage fit. 5. Anything else (no map, no category given for this weapon on this unit, a category the map leaves out, or different categories against different targets): the family's default damage, with two exceptions, checked in this order and used only when the family allows the type. Armour-piercing when the sources say the weapon is built to kill vehicles or armour, or give it a bonus against armoured targets. Explosive when it is built mainly to bring down aircraft, or its hit is a blast that hurts an area. Area damage is also the splash trait, so a shell can be armour-piercing and splash at once.' Append to the damage-types list description: 'On a researched unit, pick a weapon's type with the steps under armament[].damage in docs/fields.md.'
proposals.expected: Terror Drone claws: the infobox gives two categories (Explosive against vehicles, Sniper against infantry), so step 5 gives the blades default, melee, for A, B (one entry, see delivery-field-rule) and C. B's and C's blades atypicals disappear. Stasis ray: step 2 gives emp for all three, once the family is emp (see emp-vs-magnetic). IFV launcher: no source gives its category, so step 5 applies; built mainly against aircraft gives explosive for A, B and C. B may not assume 'Rocket', because the category must be given for this weapon. IW laser: the IFV table gives Gun, so step 4 gives kinetic for A, B and C. All three record weapon-families:laser allowed.damage-types kinetic (A changes). Tankbuster laser: no category is given for this result, so step 5 gives the laser default, energy (all). Hammer cannon: Cannon gives armour-piercing (all). Leech beam: Magic is not in the map, so it takes the drain default, energy (all). SC2 tank-mode guns: no map; a bonus against Armored gives armour-piercing (all). Siege shell: artillery does not allow armour-piercing; it is an area blast, so explosive with splash (all). Battlefield: Hydra and smart rockets explosive, chin cannon explosive, heat seekers explosive (built against aircraft); TOW, laser-guided and TV missiles armour-piercing (built to kill vehicles). All as coded. CoH rifles kinetic. Main weapon.damage reaches 100%.
proposals.side_effects: Rebuild docs/fields.md and docs/vocabularies.md. Registry notes that name an exception (RA1: heals are repair; Tempest Rising: lasers are energy; MechWarrior: flamers are fire; PS2: VS lasers are kinetic) become step 3 and stay valid. Risk in scope: step 4 will produce predictable atypicals where a map gives a type the family does not allow. Foxhole 'Anti-Tank Explosive' and DoW2 'explosive_pvp' both map to armour-piercing, so anti-tank grenades, sticky bombs and mines (explosives family: explosive, emp, fire) would each record an atypical. Review those two map entries, or decide whether explosives may take armour-piercing, before the research run. The step-5 exceptions apply only when the family allows the type, so a laser built to kill tanks stays energy, which is the intended near match.

proposals.evidence: Unclear-rule notes from A-ra3, B-ra3 (twice) and C-ra3 say nothing tells whether the ra3 damage_map binds the damage field or only hints. B and C followed it (claws explosive, IW laser kinetic); A did not (claws melee, IW laser energy). A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 flag the Leech Beam's Magic category as missing from the map. C-battlefield notes that Battlefield has no map at all.
proposals.root_cause: The registry side of the damage rule is silent. The damage_map description gives no precedence, unmapped categories have no instruction, and per-game exception notes (Tempest Rising, MechWarrior) are not marked as exceptions, so they read like competing general rules.
proposals.target: schemas/game.schema.json $defs.game.properties.damage_map.description; research/registry-notes/games-r1.md (RA3 section); research/registry-notes/games-r3.md (Tempest Rising damage bullet); research/registry-notes/games-r6.md (MechWarrior damage bullet)
proposals.change: damage_map description: 'The game's own damage categories mapped to our damage types. When the sources cited for a unit give one of its weapons a single category from this map, the mapped type is that weapon's damage, even if the weapon's family does not allow it; record the break as atypical (step 4 under armament[].damage). A category left out of the map, or a weapon with different categories against different targets, is decided by step 5.' games-r1.md, RA3: add the bullet 'Magic (the Leech Beam's category, which hurts every armour type in full) is left out of the map on purpose: weapons with it take their family's default damage.' games-r3.md, Tempest Rising lasers, and games-r6.md, MechWarrior flamers: add 'This is a named exception to the map (step 3 under armament[].damage).'
proposals.expected: All coders read one meaning from the registry: the map binds a weapon that has one stated category, and Magic falls to the family default. The Hammer leech beam stays energy for A, B and C. The claws and the IW laser resolve as in damage-decision-order.
proposals.side_effects: Rebuild docs (Game section of fields.md). The registry notes are research guidance, so the round-2 coder brief must point to them. No data in data/games.json changes.

proposals.evidence: main weapon.family 77.8% (below 80%): IFV launcher A rockets, B guided-missiles, C rockets (reference rockets). Helicopter smart/guided rockets: A and C coded guided-missiles + projectile + homing and recorded weapon-families:guided-missiles allowed.weapon-delivery projectile; B left them out. Javelin result: A rockets, B and C guided-missiles with lock-on (reference rockets). armament.delivery: B and C add lock-on on the IFV. Part of atypical rules at 68.5%. Hesitations or gaps in 6 of 12 reports (A-battlefield, A-ra3, B-battlefield gap, B-ra3, C-battlefield, C-ra3). Unclear-rule notes from A-, B- and C-battlefield and C-ra3.
proposals.root_cause: Contradiction. The weapon-families description sends any missile 'that steers, by itself or by the player's hand' to guided-missiles, but that family allows only lock-on or guided delivery, and the guided note says a shot that homes by itself is 'lock-on or the homing trait'. A self-homing rocket with no lock step therefore breaks a rule whichever way it is coded. The tie-break also turns on whether a missile steers, which RTS sources rarely say: B inferred homing from 'a dedicated anti-air launcher', A and C did not. The anti-air trait's own example (the IFV's default missiles) quietly implies rockets.
proposals.target: data/vocab/weapon-families.json: new tie_breaks entry; term descriptions of rockets and guided-missiles; list description (delete the old tie-break sentence). data/vocab/weapon-delivery.json term guided, notes (last sentence)
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [rockets, guided-missiles]; rule: 'Guided missiles only when the sources cited for the unit say the missile steers to its target: it locks on before it is fired, the shooter steers it (by wire, laser, camera or crosshair), or, in a commanded game, it homes in on or tracks its target. If they do not say it steers, it is rockets, whatever the game calls it. In a piloted game, a rocket that corrects its own course with no lock step and no warning stays rockets and takes the homing trait.' rockets description: 'Rockets or rocket pods with no lock and no steering by the shooter. Some correct their own course on the way (homing trait).' guided-missiles description: 'Missiles the sources say steer to the target: locked on before firing, steered by the shooter, or, in a commanded game, homing in on the target.' List description: delete the whole sentence that starts 'Tie-breaks:' and ends 'out-of-sight fire.' (the other tie-breaks move to tie_breaks, see family-tie-breaks-carry-over). guided notes, last sentence becomes: 'A shot that steers itself after a lock is lock-on; one that steers itself with no lock step is projectile with the homing trait.'
proposals.expected: IFV launcher: the sources do not say it steers, so rockets, projectile, explosive (B changes; A, C and the reference already agree). Main weapon family for the IFV goes to 100%. Javelin result: rockets, projectile, armour-piercing, unless the IFV's cited sources say its missiles are guided (A and the reference agree; B and C change when the sources are silent). Helicopter smart/guided rockets: piloted, self-correcting, no lock, so rockets + homing + projectile with no atypical (A and C change family; the atypical leaves both). Heat seekers (lock), TOW and TV (shooter-steered) and laser-guided missiles stay guided-missiles (all).
proposals.side_effects: In RTS games, anti-air or anti-tank missiles whose pages never say they home will be coded rockets, with the anti-air trait where they reach jets. That is acceptable: rockets and guided missiles give near-identical counter hints there. Shooter lock-on launchers (Battlefield, PS2, Foxhole) stay guided-missiles. The anti-air trait example stays true. No validator change.

proposals.evidence: main weapon.family 77.8%: helicopter A rockets (no primary; the first weapon is the Hydra pod, coded option), B rockets (primary), C autocannon (chin cannon coded primary). The family terms agree weapon by weapon; only the slot differs. armament.slot hesitations in A-, B- and C-battlefield; unclear rules on slots in multi-seat vehicles from A-, B- and C-battlefield.
proposals.root_cause: Cross-group conflict. The slot field is owned by the slots and seats group. 'primary / secondary' is unit-wide, 'option' marks loadout picks, and decision 2A (the buyer drives and fires the main weapon) is not written into the slot rule. So coders picked the gunner's gun, the pilot's pod, or no primary at all.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs.weapon.properties.slot.description and option_group.description (owned by the slots/seats group; raised here because it decides this group's main-weapon fields)
proposals.change: Add to the slot description: 'On a vehicle with several seats, the weapon the driver or pilot fires by default is primary (decision 2A). If that weapon is the default pick of a loadout group, it is still primary and carries the option_group and default: true; the other picks of that group are option. The main weapon of any other seat is secondary at most.' option_group description: 'For option weapons, and for the primary that is the default pick of a loadout group: weapons in the same group exclude each other.'
proposals.expected: Helicopter: the Hydra / S-8 rocket pods become primary for A (was option), B and C (was option). The chin cannon becomes secondary with seat gunner for C (A and B already). Main weapon family is rockets for all three, with main delivery projectile and main damage explosive.
proposals.side_effects: This must be merged with the slots group's own proposal so there is one rule. scripts/validate.mjs has no option_group checks, so no code change. The agreement script picks the first primary weapon, so it reads the new data correctly.

proposals.evidence: Where the new rules and the reference disagree. Tanya result: reference machine-gun, all three coders differ (A small-arms, B autocannon, C small-arms). Main weapon.can_target agrees with the reference only 78.3% of the time. Within the reference itself, the IW laser follows the damage map but the claws do not (resolved by damage-decision-order, which keeps both values).

proposals.target: data/units/ra3.json: ra3.allied.multigunner-ifv armament/7, armament/0, armament/1, 4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18 and armament/5; ra3.soviet.hammer-tank armament/0; then rebuild docs/samples.md

proposals.evidence: Terror Drone stasis ray: A emp, B magnetic (kinetic damage, atypical weapon-families:magnetic classes drone), C emp; reference emp. Part of the drone's armament.family set gap and of its three-way damage split (B's kinetic came from magnetic). Hesitations in A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 on family and damage; gaps in all three ('a stasis or pinning beam family').
proposals.root_cause: magnetic's description 'pull, lift or pin vehicles' matches the ray's effect word for word, while emp's 'shuts down machines' overstates a ray that leaves the target's guns working. The rule 'judged by how it behaves' then points to magnetic, which bans drones and allows only kinetic. Meanwhile the disable-machine pattern ('pin or shut down ... with an electric or EMP effect') points to emp.
proposals.target: data/vocab/weapon-families.json: new tie_breaks entry; descriptions of terms emp and magnetic. data/vocab/damage-types.json: description of term emp
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [emp, magnetic, tesla]; rule: 'EMP for any electric or electromagnetic pulse or ray whose main effect is to stop machines for a time (they can't move, can't fire, or both) while doing little or no damage; code what it stops with the root, silence or stun trait. Magnetic only for a weapon that physically pulls, lifts or drags its target. Tesla for electric arcs that do real damage.' emp (family) description: 'An electric or electromagnetic pulse or ray that stops machines and shields for a time: they can't move, can't fire, or both. Little or no damage.' magnetic description: 'Magnetic beams or harpoons that physically pull, lift or drag vehicles.' emp (damage type) description: 'Little or no damage: it stops vehicles and drones from moving, firing or both, and knocks out energy shields, for a time.'
proposals.expected: Stasis ray: family emp, damage emp (damage step 2), beam, root trait for A, B and C. B changes, and B's magnetic classes-drone atypical disappears. The drone's family set becomes {blades, emp} for all three, matching the reference.
proposals.side_effects: RA2's Magnetron and similar lift-and-drag weapons stay magnetic. Generals EMP and SupCom stun weapons stay emp. The disabler role already accepts damage:emp and weapon-trait:root. No allowed, excluded or class map changes.

proposals.evidence: CoH BAR: all three coded small-arms, but A-coh1, B-coh1 and C-coh1 hesitated (the wiki calls the BAR an LMG). IFV Tanya result: A small-arms, B autocannon, C small-arms, reference machine-gun; A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 hesitated. That makes 6 of 12 reports, and the family set disagrees on the IFV.
proposals.root_cause: The tie-break 'a soldier's personal gun is small arms, a belt-fed or mounted gun is a machine gun' sorts by where the gun sits, while the list says families are 'judged by how it behaves, not by its name'. A soldier's pistols mounted on a car are both at once: the sample took 'mounted', A and C took 'behaves', B took the name.
proposals.target: data/vocab/weapon-families.json tie_breaks (replaces the old small-arms / machine-gun clause)
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [small-arms, machine-gun]; rule: 'Judge by how it fires, not where it sits. Single shots, or short bursts from a magazine, are small arms: rifles, carbines, pistols, SMGs and automatic rifles such as the BAR. Long sustained bursts, usually belt-fed or from a rotary gun firing bullets, are a machine gun, whether a soldier carries it or it sits on a mount. A mounted weapon that the sources say copies a soldier's own gun keeps that soldier's family.'
proposals.expected: BAR: small-arms (all three, now without doubt). Tanya result: small-arms, hitscan, kinetic for A, B (changes from autocannon and projectile) and C; the sample changes from machine-gun (see sample-fixes-ra3). Conscript gatling stays machine-gun (all).
proposals.side_effects: In CoH, DoW and Battlefield, belt-fed squad weapons become machine guns and magazine-fed automatic rifles stay small arms. No validator change.

proposals.evidence: Shinobi shuriken result: A small-arms, B small-arms, C sniper; reference sniper. Gaps or hesitations in A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 (no family for thrown blades or bows). Archer Maiden bow: all three small-arms, but all three flagged that no bow family exists.
proposals.root_cause: No family names thrown blades or bows; small-arms lists only guns. sniper says 'precision shots at long range, slow to fire', and nothing says whether a one-hit infantry kill or the game's Sniper category makes a weapon a sniper.
proposals.target: data/vocab/weapon-families.json: new tie_breaks entry; description of term small-arms
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [small-arms, sniper]; rule: 'Sniper when the sources say it kills a soldier in one hit, give it the game's sniper damage category, or call it a slow, precise long-range weapon. Any other hand-held weapon is small arms.' small-arms description: 'Hand-held weapons that fire single shots or short bursts: rifles, carbines, pistols, SMGs and automatic rifles, and also bows, crossbows and thrown blades.'
proposals.expected: Shuriken: the IFV table gives Sniper damage and the sources say it kills in a hit, so sniper, projectile (thrown counts as travelling), kinetic for A and B (both change) and C; the sample is unchanged. Bow: small-arms, projectile, anti-air (all; sample unchanged). Spy and Natasha results: sniper (all).
proposals.side_effects: small-arms and sniper both allow projectile delivery, so no new atypicals. Bow and thrown-weapon units elsewhere in scope fall into these two families; no new family is needed.

proposals.evidence: SC2 siege shot: all three coded artillery, lobbed, explosive, but A-sc2, B-sc2 and C-sc2 each hesitated on family, delivery and damage (9 hesitations in 3 reports). B-sc2 gap: indirect fire with no arc. Unclear-rule notes from A-, B- and C-sc2: one judgement fixes three fields.
proposals.root_cause: 'Artillery only for arcing or out-of-sight fire' does not say whether 'out of sight' means beyond the shooter's own sight with a spotter. lobbed's description promises an arc and travel time, which the sources do not show for this shot. So the only delivery artillery allows seemed not to fit.
proposals.target: data/vocab/weapon-families.json tie_breaks (replaces the old artillery clause); data/vocab/weapon-delivery.json description of term lobbed
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [artillery, cannon]; rule: 'Artillery when the shot arcs over cover onto a ground point, or when the sources call the weapon artillery or indirect fire and it reaches further than the unit itself can see, so others must spot for it. A gun aimed straight at targets in view is a cannon, even when it reaches far.' lobbed description: 'Indirect fire: the shot arcs over cover onto a ground point, or lands on a target the shooter cannot see itself, which others must spot. Usually slow to land, often with a minimum range. It never hits fliers.'
proposals.expected: Siege shot: the wiki calls it mobile artillery and it reaches past its own sight, so artillery. lobbed now fits as written; damage is explosive by damage step 5, with splash, min-range and friendly-fire (A, B and C, now without doubt). Tank-mode guns: cannon, projectile (all).
proposals.side_effects: Long tank guns in Wargame, Broken Arrow and World in Conflict that can fire on spotted targets stay cannons, because their sources do not call them artillery. The siege role's requirement (lobbed, or range of long or more) is unaffected. lobbed keeps its allowed target types.

proposals.evidence: Helicopter chin gun: all three coded autocannon, but A-battlefield and C-battlefield hesitated (a 20 mm gatling firing exploding rounds could be autocannon, machine gun or cannon; 'no tie-break sets a calibre line'). 2 reports, no disagreement.
proposals.root_cause: The descriptions overlap: machine gun 'sustained automatic fire', autocannon 'rapid medium-calibre shells', cannon 'heavy shells'. A rotary gun firing shells matches the first two.
proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [machine-gun, autocannon, cannon]; rule: 'Machine guns fire bullets. Autocannons fire rapid shells, often exploding ones; a rotary gun firing shells is an autocannon. A cannon fires one heavy shell at a time, with a pause between shots. If the sources call the rounds shells or say they explode, it is not a machine gun. A gun copied from a soldier is settled by the small-arms rule first.'
proposals.expected: Chin gun: autocannon for A, B and C (unchanged, doubt removed). Tanya's 'autocannons' stay small-arms through the small-arms rule.
proposals.side_effects: RA3's 'Auto Cannon' damage category is a damage label, not a family test, so it is unaffected. No validator change.

proposals.evidence: Yuriko Omega result: all three coded psionic, but B-ra3 and C-ra3 flagged a gap (telekinesis, lifting and crushing, is not 'mind attacks'), and C-ra3 hesitated between psionic, emp and blades.

proposals.change: psionic description: 'Powers of the mind: control, confusion, fear, or telekinesis that lifts and crushes. Machines without a crew are immune to mind control.'
proposals.expected: Yuriko result: psionic for A, B and C (unchanged, gap closed). Structure follows the can_target rule: StrategyWiki says it can wreck a base, so it is listed with the existing psionic allowed.target-types structure atypical, as in the sample.

proposals.evidence: No disagreement. These three tie-breaks sat inside the list description next to the contradictory missile clause; moving all tie-breaks into one place avoids two sources of rules.

proposals.change: Add to tie_breaks: terms [prism, laser]; rule: 'Prism only if the beam splits or bounces to hit several targets; otherwise laser.' Terms [plasma, laser]; rule: 'Bolts that travel are plasma; light that hits at once or is held on the target is laser.' Terms [explosives, bombs]; rule: 'Charges that are placed or thrown are explosives; ordnance dropped from a flier is bombs.' (The old description sentence is deleted under rockets-vs-guided-missiles.)

proposals.evidence: Delivery hesitations in 11 of 12 reports. Source silent: A-, B- and C-coh1 (rifle hits) and A-, B- and C-sc2 (tank-mode shot) all used the family default, but no rule says to. Bark: A projectile, B projectile, C beam (reference beam); B-ra3 and C-ra3 hesitated, A-ra3 gap. IW and Tankbuster lasers: A and B hitscan, C beam (reference beam). Yuriko: A hitscan, B and C beam. Terror Drone claws: A and C one entry with attach; B split it into attach and melee entries (A-, B- and C-ra3 hesitated; B unclear rule). armament.delivery set 93.5%; the split also lowers the weapon count (61.1%).
proposals.root_cause: The delivery terms describe behaviour (travel, instant, held), but RTS sources rarely say which. There is no fallback, so 'judged by behaviour' invites guesses from fire rate or names. No rule covers one weapon that works differently on different targets.
proposals.change: New description for armament[].delivery: 'How the shot reaches the target, as the cited sources describe it. A shot seen travelling is projectile; a thrown or launched object counts. A hit that lands the moment it is fired is hitscan. A beam kept on the target, whose effect lasts or builds while it stays on, is beam. When the sources do not say which, use the family's default delivery. A rate of fire, the weapon's name or a hidden hit roll does not count as saying. One attack button is one weapon entry, even when it works differently on different targets. Code the delivery that comes first in this order: attach, ram, guided, lock-on, lobbed, drop, place, beam, projectile, hitscan, melee. Say what it does to the other targets in the summary, and list every target it can hit in can_target.'

Meaning ('can be ordered to fire at' or 'does real damage'): A-, B- and C-coh1 (rifles against vehicles and buildings), A-ra3 (Hammer cannon against infantry), B-battlefield (chin gun against jets; lock-on missile against infantry). proposals.change: New description for armament[].can_target: 'Every kind of target the weapon can be fired at and hurt in the source, even a little: weak, poor or not effective still count. Leave a type out when the sources say the weapon cannot attack it or does no damage to it, or when the source game has no such targets. A flier that can be hit only while it stands on the ground is not an air target. Piloted games (control piloted or both in data/games.json): a weapon the player aims lists every type its family allows that the game has, except high air. A lock-on weapon lists only what it can lock onto, unless the sources say it can also be fired without a lock. Commanded games: list what the sources say or show the weapon attacking. A target list that says ground means infantry, ground vehicles and structures; one that says air means low air and high air, unless the game splits its fliers and the weapon reaches only some. A weapon that latches on, drains, controls minds or disables machines lists structure only when the sources say it can attack buildings. High air and naval follow their coding rules in Target types.'

verdicts.reason: I applied the five steps to every pilot weapon. Claws give melee (two categories, so step 5). The stasis ray gives emp (step 2). The IFV launcher gives explosive (no category on the wiki table or infobox; the text says it works well against aircraft and light vehicles). The IW laser gives kinetic ('40 gun damage'). The Javelin gives armour-piercing ('Rocket'). The Peacekeeper, Spy and Shinobi give kinetic. The leech beam gives energy (Magic is not mapped). SC2 gives armour-piercing, then explosive. Battlefield comes out as coded. Five holes remain. (1) Step 1 'it heals or repairs' also catches the Hammer's leech beam: the infobox says it heals 20 HP a second while it attacks. A coder can pick repair, which drain does not allow. The step must say the weapon heals its target. (2) Step 3 'a note names this kind of weapon and a damage type' fires on notes that are hints, not rules. MechWarrior says 'Gauss rifles and large autocannons can be armour-piercing per weapon' (which autocannons?). Tempest Rising says 'the Comms Officer's laser deals Explosive damage' (energy or explosive?). TW says 'the map gives the defaults; type each weapon by what it is'. RA2 says 'choose per weapon from what it does'. Each gives two readings. Step 3 must need a firm instruction, and the notes must be rewritten (see damage-map-binding-registry). (3) The step-5 test 'built to kill vehicles' left the Battlefield Hydra open. C hesitated on 'a salvo can disable a main battle tank', and the cited Viper page says it can do devastating harm to enemy armour. Concrete words settle it as explosive: called anti-tank or anti-armour, or given a bonus against armour. (4) Generals infoboxes write INI names in words ('Armor Piercing'), so step 4 should say this counts. (5) Scope: step 4 plus families that refuse the mapped type gives predictable atypicals on ordinary units. These are explosives under Foxhole 'Anti-Tank Explosive' and DoW2 'explosive_pvp', and DoW2 lascannons and meltas (laser family, armour-piercing categories). These are fixed by explosives-allow-armour-piercing (missing) and a DoW2 note (registry revision), not here. Decisions: no conflict. The validator is unaffected: every family default sits inside its allowed list, so steps 2 and 5 never force a break.
verdicts.revised_target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json $defs.weapon.properties.damage.description (docs/fields.md armament[].damage); one sentence appended to the description of data/vocab/damage-types.json
verdicts.revised_change: New description for armament[].damage: 'What a hit does to the target. Decide in this order and stop at the first step that fits. 1. It restores health to its target: repair. A weapon that hurts its target and heals its user, such as a drain beam, is not this step. 2. It does no damage at all (it only stuns, pins, slows or marks): its family's default damage. Put the effect in traits and say in the summary that it does no damage. 3. The game's registry note tells you to record this kind of weapon as a damage type: that type. 4. The game has a damage_map in data/games.json, and the sources cited for this unit give this weapon one game damage category that the map lists: the mapped type. The same name written out in words counts. Use it even when the family's list leaves it out, and record that break in atypical. Never change the family to make the damage fit. 5. Anything else (no map, no category given for this weapon on this unit, a category the map leaves out, or different categories against different targets): the family's default damage, with two exceptions. Check them in this order, and use one only when the family allows the type. Armour-piercing when the sources call the weapon anti-tank or anti-armour, say it is built to kill vehicles, or give it a bonus against armoured targets. Explosive when it is built mainly to bring down aircraft, or its hit is a blast that hurts an area. Area damage is also the splash trait, so a shell can be armour-piercing and splash at once.' verdicts.reason: The new damage_map sentence and the RA3 Magic bullet settle A vs B/C on the claws, the IW laser and the leech beam. Taken as a general rule, that cancels step 4 for the whole game. games-r1.md RA2 says 'Choose the damage type per weapon from what it does', which is not step 5's family default. games-r3.md Tempest Rising says 'record a laser weapon as energy' but then 'The Comms Officer's laser deals Explosive damage': energy or explosive? games-r6.md MechWarrior says 'Gauss rifles and large autocannons can be armour-piercing per weapon': 'can be' is no rule, and 'large' is undefined. games-r6.md PS2 says 'VS lasers ... map to kinetic' but leaves the family open. The laser and plasma families both refuse kinetic, so every VS gun becomes atypical under step 4 ('never change the family'), or a coder picks small arms by behaviour: three readings on a third of PS2's units. Also, RA3's Spectrum category (Mirage tank) is missing from the ra3 map like Magic. DoW2 lascannons and meltas get armour-piercing categories on a laser or heat family, which makes them atypical on ordinary Space Marine and Guard units unless a note names them.

verdicts.reason: Pilot check. IFV launcher: the wiki says 'fires rockets', with no steering, so rockets for all (B changes). Smart Rockets: the cited text says 'Direct-attack self-guided', so rockets with homing and no atypical (A and C change). Heat seekers lock on, TOW and TV are steered, the laser-guided missile locks on: all stay guided missiles. The anti-air trait then lets rockets reach high air, and the anti-air rule sets the trait whenever high air is listed, so there are no new atypicals. Two holes. (2) The BF3 version of the same entry is described as 'semi-active guidance systems', which a coder can read as 'the shooter steers it (crosshair)' and so guided missiles.
